text:
nina: Follow-up to the adaptor RFC. Proposal: split "admit" (policy + signals) from "exec" (actuation). Admit returns capacity hints, staleness metadata, and an intent_id so control-plane can make conservative choices. Looking for tradeoffs.

alex: strong +1 on splitting. main worry is telemetry lag causing oscillation. how do we signal staleness and enforce safe defaults?

ryan: suggest explicit metrics_age_ms in admit response and a recommended conservative mode if metrics_age exceeds threshold. Pseudocode: 
```
if metrics_age_ms > admit.staleness_window_ms:
  decision = { admit: "conservative", capacity_hint: null }
else:
  decision = admit.decision
```

marta: rollout ops: opt-in adaptor per-tenant behind feature flag. canary 5 tenants -> synthetic traffic -> verify cost/latency delta. add billing tags for reserved vs burst so finance can reconcile.

sam: question about surface: should /admit be a declarative JSON DSL or an opaque webhook returning tokens? I'd prefer a DSL (priority bands, min/burst tokens) so operator can locally simulate and test.

infra-bot: deploybot: canary deployed autoscale-adaptor v0.2 to staging :rocket:

alex: also consider heterogeneous GPU clusters + preemptible nodes: admit should include gpu_type hints and eviction_risk (0..1) so control-plane can avoid short-lived placements. suggested_ttl helps too.

nina: draft admit response shape idea: 
```
{ admit: "allow|deny|conservative", reason: "string", metrics_age_ms: 1200, capacity_hints: ["A100","H100"], eviction_risk: "0.25", suggested_ttl_sec: 300 }
```
I'll tidy names.

ryan: add intent_id UUID on admit for traceability. Observability: histograms for admit_latency_ms and decision_changes_per_minute.

marta: runbook: operator unreachable -> control-plane falls back to local conservative policy and alerts #eng-oncall. include playbook steps (restart operator, failover to warmpool, notify tenant owner). :thumbsup:

sam: I'll sketch DSL examples later. sample: `{ priority: "latency", weight: 0.8, min_tokens: 20, burst_tokens: 10 }`	want to validate semantics with runtime.

alex: must enumerate allowed failure modes in the doc (control-plane slow, operator crash, partial connectivity). prefer conservative admits biased to availability.

nina: next steps: proto + unit tests PR by EOD Wed. reviewers: @alex @sam. I'll post an updated design doc to https://redwood.internal/rfcs/admit-exec-adaptor (WIP) and include failure-mode matrix and rollout plan.

ryan: one more: rate-limit admit calls per-tenant and include backoff hint to avoid thundering herd during reconnects.

marta: also include a compatibility shim so older operators ignore new fields gracefully.

nina: great feedback. I'll update the RFC and ping reviewers. keep thread focused here. thanks all!
